title: Rooms, apartments — and their own subpages
body:
You reach the room module's settings screen on the Modules tab, with the **„Setting”** link next to the module.
Here you enter which rooms and apartments you rent out, and what guests should know about them.

Important: the booking calendar and the pricing use these same rooms — it is enough to maintain them in one place,
and they will match everywhere. Once the rooms are in place and you want to give them prices, you do not have to
search: at the top of the screen, below the introductory text (beside it on a computer), the **„Edit prices and seasons”** button
takes you straight to the price module's settings screen. If the Prices module is not switched on yet, the button
reads **„Enable pricing module”** and takes you to the Modules tab — there, on the Prices, seasons card, put it in your basket with the
**„Add to cart”** button and finalise it in the basket.

![Screenshot: the introductory line at the top of the screen, with the “Edit prices, seasons” button below it](assets/hu/arak-gomb.png)

![Screenshot: the rooms grid on a phone](assets/hu/screen.png)

## What is where on the screen?

The screen's title is the module's name, above it the **„Back to modules”** link, below the title the module's fee and the
**„Guide to this screen”** button. Below the introductory note is a row of small buttons: **„The whole house”**
(if you have several rooms), **„Its rooms”**, **„Add a new room”** and **„Rules”**. With a single room, the row's
two buttons are **„What does it output?”** and **„Rules”**. This row stays at the top of the screen while you scroll, tapping a button jumps the page to that part, and the button for the part
you are in is always highlighted. On a computer the same list sits on the far right, titled **„On this page”**.

## The rooms grid

Under the **„Its rooms”** heading each of your rooms appears on a card, and the card shows exactly
what the guest sees on the website: the **cover photo**, the name, the capacity. At the bottom right of the photo the
badge shows the number of photos, and with a single photo the word **„Details”** — because “1 photo” would promise
a gallery. Below the name is the status: **„Has its own page”** or **„Incomplete”**.

If the same photo is the cover of two rooms, the card says so with a red badge and names the
other room — so it cannot happen unnoticed that two rooms appear on the website with the same
photo.

You add a new room by tapping the dashed-frame **„Add a new room”** strip at the bottom of the page:
a highlighted box opens, where you enter the name and the capacity, and press the
**„Add”** button. The box is closed by default so that it does not get mixed up with the existing ones: your
existing rooms are above it, in the card grid, and you edit them by tapping their card. If you rent out the whole property only as one unit,
a single room is enough — in that case the guest never even sees a room choice.

When you add the **second** unit, your one unit so far is usually the property itself
(on a new account this is the default, named “The entire property”): this stays **the whole house**, and the one you just added
becomes your first room. In that case there is no question.

If you renamed this single unit earlier, only you know what it is. Then, in the same
form, directly above **„Add”**, a question awaits, calling it by its name: **„Mi az eddigi
„…”?”** You can choose between two answers:

- **„The whole house”**: it stays the whole house, and the one you just added becomes your first room.
- **„My first room”**: the existing unit becomes a room (its calendar, photos and price are kept), and the whole
  house is added separately by the system, without a price.

If you skip it, a red line below the button tells you what is missing, and the question is highlighted in red —
choose, and press the button again. If a named room is left on its own (for example after a
deletion), there is no question: it stays a room.

If the Prices module is switched on too (and you do not rent out the house only as one unit), BEFORE pressing **„Add”** you can also
enter the price here (**„Base price”** field), or tick the box below it: **„I won't set a price — I'll send a custom quote”**.
Neither is required; the room is added either way. If we cannot interpret the
price you typed (for example you wrote it in letters), the room is added without a price, and the yellow
line says so too. If there is neither a price nor a tick, after saving a yellow line says
that the room has been added but has no price. Next to it, the **„Set a price”** button takes you to the Pricing page, and the
**„I won't set a price”** button records on the spot that you will send an individual offer.

## The editor: tap the card

Tapping the card opens the editor in a pop-up. You can close it with the **×** at the top left, by tapping the
dark background next to the pop-up or with the `Esc` key. The **„Save”** button stays at the bottom of the pop-up
the whole time, so you do not have to scroll down for it. It has three tabs:

### “Basics”

Here, in one place, are the room's **name**, its **capacity** and its **description** — a few sentences about what
characterises this room and what guests love about it. On a computer you see on the right, straight away,
the card the guest will get.

The capacity is also the upper limit for bookings: a guest cannot request a booking for more people than this in this
room. If you lower it later, for a request already received for more people a warning on the **„Bookings”** tab
flags the difference.

### “Images”

At the top, the **cover photo** is shown large, with the caption **„This is what the website shows on this card”**.
This is the photo the guest sees on the room's card.

With the **„Upload image”** button you can upload photos from here, from the room, too. The uploaded photo goes into the
**house's shared photo library**, and we assign it to this room straight away as well — so it is enough to upload a photo
once, even if you want to show it for several rooms. If the room had no cover photo
yet, the first one uploaded becomes the cover; if it had one, we do not overwrite it.

If we cannot accept a file (not JPEG/PNG/WEBP, or larger than 6 MB), we tell you
**which file** was left out and **why** — the rest are uploaded anyway.

Below that comes **„The property's shared gallery”**, containing all the property's photos. The faded photos do not
belong to this room yet.

* the **tick** (top left corner) assigns the photo to this room — it is recorded when you save;
* the **star** (bottom right corner) makes it the cover photo. If the photo did not belong to this
  room yet, the star assigns it too, and we say so.

If you remove a photo from the room (untick it, then save), the photo **stays in the shared
library** — it is not deleted. If it was the cover photo, the next one in line takes its place; if no
photo is left, we tell you that too.

### “Amenities”

Here you list what is **in this room** (items for the whole house are set in the
Amenities module). The selected items appear as small tags; you add new ones in the
**„Add from list”** section, on tiles with icons. If no item is selected yet,
the list is open straight away. Typing into the search field finds anything quickly (e.g. “jetty”). Anything not
on the list you can type into the **„Other, not on the list”** field, one per line. Whatever you have already ticked
for the whole house in the Amenities module (e.g. wifi, breakfast) can be selected here too, and
its tile shows a small caption: **„for the whole property too”**. Feel free to tick it for the room as well —
on the room's own page the guest reads only the room's list.

This tab can only be edited if the **Amenities** module is switched on — if it is not, the tab
shows what you could set here and invites you to the Modules tab.

![Screenshot: the “Photos” tab with the shared photo library](assets/hu/picker.png)

## When does a room get its own page?

If a room has at least **one assigned photo** AND **a description or amenities**, the
room gets its own subpage on your website — search engines (Google) can find it separately, which can bring more
guests. On the grid card and on the **„Basics”** tab we always show whether that
room will have its own page, and if not, what is missing. We never create an empty page — it
would do more harm than good.

## The whole house

If you have more than one room, a separate card titled **„The whole house”** stands above the grid. This is not
one of your rooms but the house itself: here you decide how you rent it out.

The card has a single box: **„Rented as a whole only”**. If it is not ticked (this is the default): the guest books room by room — one room in a request,
several, or even all of them. In that case the whole house has **no separate price**, and you do not need to enter one:
anyone who wants the whole house selects every room and pays the rooms' prices (listed room by room,
with the total at the end). A sentence on the card says so.

If you tick the **„Rented as a whole only”** box: the guest can only book the
whole house. The rooms get a “for display only” mark on the grid: on the website they appear with photos and amenities, but without price or booking. In that case we ask for a price
only for the house — on the Prices page the rooms have no card, and we do not mention the missing price either among the
tasks or by email. The tick saves by itself.

The card also shows:

- how many rooms and how many people belong to the house; tapping the **„Images, description”** link opens the house's
  own editor (photos, description, amenities);
- **only in “as one unit” mode** you enter the house's price here (if the Prices module is switched on): the
  **„Base price:”** line shows the current one; type the new one into the field and press the
  **„Save price”** button. If you save it empty, the price is deleted and the guest requests a quote. If the tick is not
  on, this field does not even appear — since the house's price follows from the prices of the selected rooms.

With a single room the card does not appear — in that case there is nothing to decide.

## How does a guest book several rooms at once?

On your website, in the booking section, the guest:

1. first selects the arrival and departure days in the calendar. Until then, in place of the room list it
   says: “First choose the days — then we will show you which room is free.” The calendar shows a
   night as booked only if **none** of the rooms is free that night;
2. then every room appears in the “Which rooms would you like to book?” list. Next to the free rooms
   is the price for the whole stay (where there is no price, “individual price”), and they can be selected
   with a tick. A booked room is grey, labelled “Booked for this period”, and cannot be selected;
3. ticks rooms one by one, or requests all of them with one button: “I'd like all … free rooms”, or, if
   every room is free, “I'd like all … rooms (the whole house)”. The “Clear selection” button
   removes everything;
4. the price is shown item by item per room, with the total below. The upper limit of guests is the sum of the
   selected rooms' capacities.

You receive this as **one** request on the **„Bookings”** tab, listing the rooms. You confirm or decline
all of them at once — there is no half-and-half. The details are in the Bookings tab's
help.

## Deleting a room

You can delete any room with the **„Delete room”** button at the bottom of its pop-up. The whole house
only when you have just one room left — with several rooms the server refuses: “The whole house cannot be
deleted while you have several rooms.” The button does not delete straight away:
a confirmation opens below it, asking about the room by name and listing what is lost
with it: **„Deleted permanently along with the room:”** the days closed in its calendar, the base price and the
seasonal prices, the calendar sync (with the portal's name) and earlier, completed bookings — each with
a count. The room's photos stay in the gallery. If you are sure, press the **„Yes, delete it”**
button; if you have changed your mind, the **„Cancel”** button. Deletion cannot be undone.

In three cases the room cannot be deleted. For the last room the button does not even appear. If a
booking request for the room is still awaiting your decision, or one of your offers is awaiting the guest's reply, in place of the confirmation
there is a yellow-framed notice: it shows the request's reference, period and the guest's name, and the
**„Bookings”** button takes you to where you can decide on it. That way the guest is not left without an answer. The same
notice appears if an accepted booking that has not yet ended belongs to the room.

If after the deletion you have a single room left, that room **stays a room**: if you add a new one later,
the form asks nothing, and next to the two rooms the system adds the whole house by itself, without a
price. You only need to give the house a price if you tick the **„Rented as a whole only”** box —
then you enter it on the house's card.
